chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Khalid al-Kufi, raising it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Worship consists of seventy parts, the best of which is seeking the halal (permissible livelihood)."

key_terms.اَلْعِبَادَةُ: Worship or devotion, broadly defined here to include daily activities like earning a living.
key_terms.سَبْعُونَ جُزْئاً: Seventy parts, indicating a comprehensive and multifaceted nature of worship.
key_terms.طَلَبُ الْحَلاَلِ: Seeking the halal (permissible), specifically referring to the pursuit of lawful livelihood and income.

ai.seo_question: What is the highest form of worship according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi places this narration within the chapter of trade (*al-Makasib*), highlighting the Shia juristic view that securing lawful sustenance is a foundational act of worship. By elevating *talab al-halal* above the other sixty-nine aspects, the Imam underscores that economic independence prevents reliance on others and enables sincere devotion, a concept deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition of self-sufficiency.
